one_line: Safely migrates recurring calendar events while preserving future exceptions and validating serialized ICS invariants.
what_it_does: Loads an ICS calendar, simulates SeriesSafe and conventional recurrence edits, shows losses, validates nine invariants, and gates commit until checks pass.
leverage_rationale: The structured WebMCP surface exposes calendar graph state, simulation, byte-level validation, and guarded commit; a general UI-driving agent could not reliably preserve and prove recurrence exceptions comparably well.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes eight tool calls to load, inspect, simulate, validate, and commit.
Nine invariants are checked against serialized ICS bytes before the commit tool appears.
The app runs locally in-tab without an account or server.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent end-to-end workflow with risk comparison, refusal behavior, validation, and commit, although image inspection was unavailable.
execution_evidence: Transcript reports both outcomes, five preserved customizations, refusal when the requested end-date constraint cannot be met, and successful commit.
Facts show a live demo, public repository, and 168-second video.
Frame and screenshot evidence was required but could not be visually analyzed due to vision rate limiting.
impact_rationale: Recurring-event exception loss is a concrete, costly problem for teachers and organizations, and the product directly provides proof-preserving migration.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets moving recurring events without losing cancellations, make-ups, and room changes.
Transcript gives a realistic language-school calendar scenario and explicit platform failure mode.
creativity_rationale: It combines recurrence-graph transformation, side-by-side counterfactual simulation, byte-level invariants, and capability gating into a memorable safety-oriented calendar workflow.
creativity_evidence: The product refuses unsafe requests rather than producing unverifiable calendars.
Commit capability is conditionally registered only after validation.
usability_note: Natural-language intent, visible proof, refusal, and no-login local workflow are strong usability choices.
red_flags: Visual frame evidence could not be independently inspected because vision service returned rate-limit errors.
standouts: Byte-level invariant validation and safety-gated commit.
Clear counterfactual comparison against conventional calendar behavior.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and a well-evidenced, high-value workflow.

one_line: Evidence desk where agents draft and validate vulnerability reports while humans control approval and export.
what_it_does: Manages synthetic vulnerability cases, evidence-bound report drafts, deterministic validation, review gates, approval, and Markdown export.
leverage_rationale: Structured case, evidence, validation, and draft operations let agents work against exact security evidence while keeping approval outside the agent surface; UI automation would be brittle and less provenance-safe.
leverage_evidence: About text defines agent tools for listing cases, inspecting rules/evidence, drafting, validating, and requesting review.
Approval and export are intentionally not agent tools.
Agent and human edits appear in one workspace without reload.
execution_rationale: The seeded workspace has differentiated cases and explicit blocked/approved states, suggesting a complete scoped workflow, but there is no submitted video and visual evidence could not be inspected.
execution_evidence: RL-101, RL-102, and RL-103 exercise positive, missing-evidence, and out-of-scope paths.
About text describes exact revision approval and invalidation after later edits.
Facts show a live demo and public repository.
impact_rationale: Security report accuracy and evidence traceability are real needs for vulnerability programs; the product directly addresses overclaiming and human accountability.
impact_evidence: Problem statement identifies unsupported impact, out-of-scope assets, and overstatement at the evidence/claim boundary.
Human approval and export control are explicit.
creativity_rationale: The editorial evidence-desk framing and evidence-bound review gate are a fresh synthesis of agent assistance and security reporting.
creativity_evidence: Four evidence signals are bound to the exact report revision awaiting approval.
Synthetic cases deliberately model distinct evidence deficiencies.
usability_note: Clear seeded cases and visible review blocking support investigation, though UI proof was unavailable.
red_flags: No video submitted; visual evidence could not be inspected.
standouts: Approval/export separation and revision invalidation preserve meaningful human control.
advance_reason: Strong practical agent-human workflow with credible security-reporting impact.

one_line: Human-agent cybersecurity investigation workspace for evidence-linked findings and review routing.
what_it_does: Discovers incidents, retrieves structured evidence, proposes linked findings with confidence and next actions, and routes every agent finding to human review.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent structured incident and evidence access and creates traceable findings, while review remains outside the tool surface; this is materially safer than UI inference.
leverage_evidence: About text states autonomous discovery and invocation of incident discovery, evidence retrieval, and finding creation tools.
Findings carry evidence IDs and enter pending-human-review.
No WebMCP approval or rejection tool exists.
execution_rationale: The described central flow is coherent and includes a meaningful review loop, but the packet lacks video and visual inspection was unavailable.
execution_evidence: Natural-language investigation leads through discovery, retrieval, and finding creation.
Human can approve, reject, or request more evidence.
Facts show live demo, public repo, and five gallery images.
impact_rationale: Incident analysts need evidence-backed conclusions and reviewable provenance; the product addresses a real high-stakes workflow.
impact_evidence: Problem framing distinguishes evidence, inference, and validated conclusions.
Human investigator can challenge conclusions that exceed evidence.
creativity_rationale: The evidence-linked pending-review model is a thoughtful human-agent interaction pattern, though the domain and workflow are established.
creativity_evidence: Findings link to specific evidence IDs and include confidence and review controls.
Review is structurally separated from agent capabilities.
usability_note: Natural-language discovery plus explicit human review is understandable and safety-oriented.
red_flags: No video submitted; visual evidence could not be inspected.
standouts: Evidence-linked findings with a real request-more-evidence loop.
advance_reason: Credible high-stakes use case and strong agent/human boundary.

one_line: Semantic release testing for WebMCP catalogs that verifies agent choices against trusted site effects.
what_it_does: Ingests live catalogs, defines representative requests and expected effects, runs fresh-agent cases, and diagnoses wrong tools, arguments, or missing effects.
leverage_rationale: The product tests the semantic gap that ordinary handler tests and UI automation miss, using live agent choice plus trusted state/effect verification.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes comparison of chosen tool and canonical arguments with trusted website state and operation ledger.
It detects a successful handler with no required effect and wrong-tool selection.
Cases support independent regressions and stateful journeys.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete define-arm-test-verify-diagnose-save-rerun loop with baseline, planted fault, semantic collision, and integrity cases.
execution_evidence: Video facts show live demo, public repo, 154-second video, and 15 gallery images.
Transcript reports baseline pass, planted fault detection, seven-request journey, 24-case snapshot, and invocation integrity cases.
Expected answers remain hidden from the fresh agent.
impact_rationale: Incorrect agent actions are a central deployment risk for WebMCP sites, and this tool offers a concrete release-quality control.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets tools that return success but do the wrong thing.
It verifies actual site changes rather than trusting return status.
creativity_rationale: Semantic release testing treats meaning as the unit under test and separates semantic behavior from invocation integrity, a notably original infrastructure concept.
creativity_evidence: Fresh-agent testing uses live catalog and request semantics rather than predetermined tool calls.
Controlled semantic variation and observed effects are saved as contracts.
usability_note: Quickstart and explicit release loop make a complex testing problem operational, though setup includes a private expiring command.
red_flags: Visual frame evidence could not be independently inspected because vision service returned rate-limit errors.
standouts: Tests agent semantics, not merely schema or handler correctness.
Trusted effect verification catches silent success.
advance_reason: One of the strongest packets: high WebMCP-specific leverage, complete evidence, and clear impact.

one_line: A Taboo game where a personal agent receives forbidden clues and converses with the player.
what_it_does: Runs a playable guessing game in which the agent privately receives a secret word and forbidden words and describes it without violating constraints.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides structured game-state and interaction tools for an agent, but a general conversational agent could reproduce much of the game with some state-management friction.
leverage_evidence: About text describes five WebMCP tools and private secret/forbidden-word state.
Pitch claims voice conversation, visualization, and cross-web/AR ambitions, but packet evidence centers on the game.
execution_rationale: The core concept is understandable and appears playable, but the packet provides no video and broad claims exceed the directly evidenced scope.
execution_evidence: Facts show a live demo, public repository, and two gallery images.
About text gives a concrete game rule and interaction loop.
No video or independently viewable frame analysis was available.
impact_rationale: It offers entertainment and a demonstrable way to make WebMCP approachable, but the practical value is mostly exploratory.
impact_evidence: Pitch explicitly frames the game as making WebMCP fun and revealing its promise.
The game provides a recognizable social guessing activity.
creativity_rationale: Using WebMCP to give an agent private constraints and play a classic verbal game is a fresh, memorable demonstration, though not deeply novel as a game.
creativity_evidence: Agent must describe without secret or forbidden words.
Voice-first personal-agent framing extends beyond a static tool demo.
usability_note: Simple familiar rules should be approachable; voice and multi-surface claims are not fully evidenced.
red_flags: Broad AR/cross-web claims are not substantiated by the packet.
No video submitted and images could not be inspected.
standouts: A playful, legible demonstration of agent-mediated game state.
advance_reason: Interesting demonstration but weaker evidence and lower demonstrated impact than the strongest submissions.

one_line: A stateful text adventure where an AI Dungeon Master acts only through five WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Lets players explore, fight, talk, and issue free-form actions while the agent reads state, spawns encounters, resolves combat, awards items, and advances story.
leverage_rationale: The agent operates a real game state through constrained tools and can be refused, making WebMCP materially more than narration or UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Pitch says five registered tools are the only agent entry points and the page can refuse them.
About text distinguishes real underlying state from model narration and lists concrete state-changing tools.
Tool refusals enforce game rules such as no second fight while one is active.
execution_rationale: The packet presents multiple coherent scenarios including combat, difficulty, rewards, authored rooms, ending, and phone layout, but no video and no visual inspection.
execution_evidence: Seven gallery scenarios are named, including broken gate, spawned fight, reward, authored room, ending, and phone.
Facts show a live demo, public repository, and seven gallery images.
No video submitted.
impact_rationale: It offers credible entertainment and a useful demonstration of bounded agent agency in games; the audience is clear even if niche.
impact_evidence: Pitch and about text identify the familiar AI-DM problem of invented or forgotten state.
Playable text adventure and refusal behavior directly address consistency.
creativity_rationale: Making the agent a constrained operator rather than an omnipotent narrator, with refusal as a first-class mechanic, is an original interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Real game rules, dice/state underneath, and five exclusive tools constrain the DM.
The page can refuse invalid agent actions.
usability_note: Buttons plus free-form play and explicit refusal likely make the loop legible, though visual proof was unavailable.
red_flags: No video submitted; visual evidence could not be inspected.
standouts: Refusal and underlying game state make the agent a participant constrained by the rules.
advance_reason: Strong, category-neutral WebMCP interaction concept with credible execution evidence.

one_line: Agent-ready flood simulation lab for running, replaying, inspecting, and comparing urban scenarios.
what_it_does: Provides terrain and solver inspection, scenario setup, long-running simulation, replay, depth/speed sampling, affected-location focus, and comparisons across Houston and Chennai study areas.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP coordinates a complex multi-step simulation and exposes exact state and numerical results that an agent could not safely infer from a 3D UI or animation.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes 21 endpoints covering terrain, solver, setup, run monitoring, replay, sampling, focus, and compare.
Agent reports exact depth, speed, area, arrival time, assumptions, and result identity.
About text explicitly contrasts structured state with guessing from buttons and pixels.
execution_rationale: The transcript demonstrates two scenario runs, replay, quantitative reporting, affected-place navigation, and study-area coverage; visual inspection was unavailable but packet evidence is unusually detailed.
execution_evidence: Live demo facts and transcript show Houston heavy-rain and Brays Bayou overflow workflows.
About text describes Houston and Velachery studies, assumptions, limitations, and comparisons.
Five gallery images and public repo are present.
impact_rationale: Flood scenario exploration has clear value for planners, investigators, and educators, and the product makes assumptions and limitations visible rather than presenting opaque animation.
impact_evidence: Concrete urban flood planning questions are answered with depth, speed, affected area, and arrival times.
The product addresses multi-step setup and interpretation difficulty.
creativity_rationale: The combination of replayable flood forensics, agent-safe multi-step orchestration, visible assumptions, and point sampling is ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Supports counterfactual rain, overflow, blocked-drain scenarios and comparison.
Agent can take the user to the first affected location at its arrival time.
usability_note: Conversational control and exact readouts simplify a complex simulation, though the domain remains inherently dense.
red_flags: Transcript labels results as planning preview numbers; not a substitute for validated operational forecasting.
standouts: Exact replay/readout workflow over a complex visual simulation.
Assumptions, limitations, and result identities are part of the product output.
advance_reason: High-leverage, high-impact, ambitious agent workflow with strong packet evidence.

one_line: Shared qualitative-research canvas where agents surface contested quotes and humans make the interpretive decision.
what_it_does: Lets researchers organize themes and quotes while an agent reads the corpus, identifies ambiguous assignments, ranks disputes, and presents them without being able to settle them.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent shared document state and a provenance-preserving mutation path while structurally preventing it from resolving contested interpretation; generic UI driving would weaken auditability.
leverage_evidence: Agent works on the same document and its operations appear in one authored log.
The agent lacks any capability to settle a contested quote.
About text emphasizes shared live state and no backdoor.
execution_rationale: The core human-agent loop is coherent and intentionally bounded, but evidence is description plus one gallery image, no video, and visual analysis was unavailable.
execution_evidence: About text specifies corpus reading, contest ranking, presentation, and human drag decisions.
Facts show a live demo and one gallery image, but no public repository and no video.
impact_rationale: Qualitative researchers have a real volume-versus-interpretation problem, and preserving disagreement and provenance can materially improve defensibility.
impact_evidence: Problem statement identifies clerical coding burden and the importance of ambiguous quotes.
Human retains the analytical decision and audit trail.
creativity_rationale: Treating disagreement as the output to escalate rather than noise to resolve is a distinctive interaction model with strong methodological coherence.
creativity_evidence: Agent ranks contested quotes and stops at the human decision boundary.
One shared authored log records researcher and agent operations.
usability_note: Direct canvas manipulation plus surfaced disputes fits researchers, though dense corpus workflows may need onboarding.
red_flags: No video and only one gallery image; end-to-end operation is claimed rather than observed.
standouts: The agent is designed to surface ambiguity, not erase it.
Authorship and provenance are treated as product functionality.
advance_reason: Distinctive, high-value research workflow despite thinner evidence.

one_line: Voice-first clinical memory layer that exposes patient history and documentation to agents.
what_it_does: Captures patient and consultation conversations, converts them to structured clinical context, and lets agents retrieve histories, draft SOAP notes, and flag red symptoms.
leverage_rationale: Structured access can reduce form and tab switching, but the packet does not establish that WebMCP is indispensable versus an API or careful UI automation, and clinical safety constraints are underdeveloped.
leverage_evidence: About text describes agent retrieval of patient history and drafting/flagging operations.
Existing platform already had structured clinical memory before WebMCP was added.
No frame sheets or video were submitted.
execution_rationale: The claimed product scope is broad, but there is no visual/video evidence and no gallery images, so end-to-end execution is thinly evidenced.
execution_evidence: Facts show a live demo and public repository.
About text describes patient conversation, consultation transcription, summaries, SOAP notes, triage, and agent access.
No submitted frames or screenshot analysis beyond the required but unavailable image.
impact_rationale: Clinical memory and reduced repeated history-taking address a serious, specific healthcare need, though the packet does not prove safe clinical deployment.
impact_evidence: Problem statement identifies lost patient context and clinician documentation burden.
Outputs include history, SOAP notes, summaries, triage, and red flags.
creativity_rationale: Continuous patient memory plus agent-accessible clinical context is a meaningful healthcare synthesis, though the underlying pattern is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Voice-first patient and consultation experiences are combined with direct structured agent access.
The project frames memory continuity across providers as the central concept.
usability_note: Voice-first interaction may reduce data-entry burden, but clinical review, consent, and error handling are not evidenced.
red_flags: No frame sheets and no gallery images; execution cannot be visually checked.
High-stakes medical claims lack demonstrated safety, consent, or clinician verification details in the packet.
standouts: Clear real-world need for longitudinal clinical memory.
advance_reason: Potential impact is high, but WebMCP delta and actual execution are insufficiently evidenced for advancement.

one_line: Local-first visual analytics canvas shared by humans and WebMCP agents through one action dispatcher.
what_it_does: Imports local tabular data, queries with DuckDB-Wasm, creates charts and metrics, filters/transforms/highlights data, annotates, and supports undo/redo for both UI and agent actions.
leverage_rationale: The shared live analytical state and common dispatcher make agent changes visible, reversible, and composable with human work; general UI driving would be less reliable for structured data exploration.
leverage_evidence: About text says UI and WebMCP use one action dispatcher and undo/redo spans both.
Agent can inspect datasets, analyze, create/update visualizations, filter, highlight, define metrics, and annotate.
Local-first architecture avoids backend/auth dependency.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a broad but coherent local analytics workspace and multiple demo variants, though no video and visual inspection was unavailable.
execution_evidence: Facts show live demo, public repo, and three gallery images.
About text lists CSV/TSV/JSON/NDJSON import, DuckDB-Wasm analysis, charts, matrices, line/donut/bar demos, and history.
No video submitted.
impact_rationale: Local, collaborative exploratory analytics has a broad identifiable audience and directly reduces friction between human analysis and agent assistance.
impact_evidence: Use cases include importing, exploring, charting, filtering, transforming, and annotating datasets.
Shared state prevents separate agent and human versions of an analysis.
creativity_rationale: The local-first shared canvas and single dispatcher unify agent and human analytics in a concrete, technically coherent interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent-created charts are normal workspace visualizations and remain editable.
Undo/redo crosses the human-agent boundary.
usability_note: Local file support, visible shared canvas, and reversible actions are strong usability choices; no visual verification was possible.
red_flags: No video submitted; visual evidence could not be inspected.
standouts: One dispatcher and shared undo/redo make the collaboration model tangible.
Local-first design avoids account and backend friction.
advance_reason: Strong shared-state WebMCP use case with credible execution and clear audience value.
